authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: Don't replace the cage-toolbox identity with a tournament cEDH shell (verification L37).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: Without Mairsil the caged abilities are inaccessible.
Graveyard hate stops caging from the yard.
Self-mill lines like Mirror-Mad Phantasm were cut as unsafe.

value.interaction: Force of Will, Fierce Guardianship, Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, Deadly Rollick, Toxic Deluge, Cyclonic Rift.
value.mana: 32 lands, Mana Vault, Chrome Mox, Mox Diamond, Lotus Petal, Gilded Lotus.
value.protection: Lightning Greaves, Deflecting Swat, Aetherling and Cephalid Inkshrouder cages.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Mairsil is the engine: every caged ability lives on him, and five of the six Spellbook combos include him.
accepted_role.honest_note: Each acquired ability is once per turn per Mairsil object, so the loops need fresh objects (Quicksilver Elemental, blinks, copies). The deck is fragile to graveyard and exile hate on caged cards. The cycle 51 M1 review (mairsil-01..11) verifies the cage rules; mairsil-10 (Marvin without the once-per-turn limit) was re-evaluated in Bot cycle 62 under CR 113.10a: Marvin's copies keep the restriction, so the no-restriction hypothesis is incorrect (M1 post-acceptance correction, data/grixis/m1_corrections.json).
